clue.text: Where Marco Polo went in a yacht, wandering

indicators.note: something wandering does not keep a fixed course, so the letters stray into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An imagined account of the Venetian explorer drifting about in a yacht on his travels.
explanation.walkthrough: Marco Polo travelled overland, so the yacht is pure misdirection: it is the source of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the old European name for China, the land Marco Polo famously reached.

clue.text: Stream must be present

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flow of water or electricity
second meaning: belonging to now, contemporary

explanation.surface: A rule that a stream has to be there, or attending.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for a flow of water and an adjective for something happening at the present time.

clue.text: Toddler, extremely exhausted, has to be carried

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its very first and very last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of exhausted

explanation.surface: A worn-out little child needs carrying home.
explanation.definitionFit: To tote is to carry or lug something, so the past tense is a synonym of carried.

clue.text: Dismay about queen turning up in this costume

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps around the other
in a down clue, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword queen

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to see a queen arrive dressed in a certain outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: APPAL splits after its second P to take the turned-up queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing in general, and a costume is a set of clothes, so the two overlap as synonyms.

clue.text: Parisian thanks leader of allies in old kingdom

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever comes first, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A French ally offers thanks to the head of the allied forces in an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Parisian signals a French word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercia was one of the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of central England, so it is a historic realm.

clue.text: Puzzle resolved in game

indicators.note: something resolved has been worked out and put into new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle that came up during a game has been solved.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, which is a kind of puzzle.

clue.text: No curates could reform a kept woman

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: No clergyman, it seems, could save a mistress from her way of life.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures curates reforming a sinner; reform is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a mistress supported by wealthy lovers, so she is a woman kept by a patron.

clue.text: Oscar-winning film produced in Australia

indicators.note: in places one word inside the letters of another

explanation.surface: A film that won an Academy Award was made in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as trivia about where a film was shot; produced and Australia are both wordplay, with one sitting inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Amadeus, the 1984 film about Mozart, won the Academy Award for Best Picture.

clue.text: A retiring band prepared to be stoical

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready and set up afresh, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A shy group of musicians gets ready to endure their ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to put up with hardship cheerfully, which is to accept it without complaint.

clue.text: Worry about moving into empty flat

indicators.note: moving into puts one piece inside another, like a new tenant
empty means the inside of the word is cleared out, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of flat

explanation.surface: Someone frets over moving into an unfurnished flat.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious, so it is a synonym of the verb worry.

clue.text: Fastidious individual

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fussy, hard to please
second meaning: specific, single, not general

explanation.surface: A fussy person, described in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both fussy about details and relating to one specific thing as opposed to others.

clue.text: Sex object in Germany taking off a lot

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the letters of another
taking off means removing something, so letters are cut away

parts.note: an end is an aim or object

explanation.surface: A sex object in Germany is taking off a lot of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Germany loses many to leave GER, which then holds END. Sex object looks like one phrase; sex is the definition and object the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Gender is used as a synonym of sex in classifying people as male or female.

clue.text: Never mind vacuum?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: it is of no importance
second meaning, read literally: an absence of any substance

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading: a vacuum is space with no matter in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive idiom meaning it does not matter, and literally describes empty space containing no substance.

clue.text: Excursion occupying shy lad

indicators.note: occupying means sitting inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to sling

explanation.surface: A day out is giving a timid boy something to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy looks like an adjective for the lad, but here it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripling is a youth not yet fully grown, so a young lad.

clue.text: Hints from close friends

definitions.meaning: first meaning: suggests indirectly, a verb
second meaning: people one is very close to, a noun

explanation.surface: Pointers passed on by one's best mates.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning suggests indirectly and a plural noun for very close companions, pronounced differently.

clue.text: Snakes like empty pockets

indicators.note: empty means the inside of the word is cleared out, keeping only its outside letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of pockets

explanation.surface: Snakes are fond of pockets with nothing in them.
explanation.walkthrough: Like looks like a verb meaning enjoy, but it is the comparison word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asps are small venomous snakes, so the plural fits snakes.

clue.text: Walton loses points as a singer

indicators.note: something that loses pieces has them taken away, so letters are removed

explanation.surface: The composer Walton is marked down for his performance as a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Points are compass points, here W and N, removed from either end of Walton.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice, so a type of singer.

clue.text: A learner with a gun, possibly frightened

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a UK car

explanation.surface: A novice carrying a firearm might well be scared.
explanation.walkthrough: L stands for learner because UK learner drivers display an L plate.
explanation.definitionFit: To be alarmed is to be suddenly afraid, a close synonym of frightened.

clue.text: Fix it on beast like a mule

indicators.note: to fix is to put right by rearranging, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to load something onto an animal, a mule perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The beast in the surface is the mule; beast is fodder and mule part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are proverbially stubborn, so being like a mule is being obstinate.

clue.text: Deliberation even if on time

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Careful consideration, even when time is short.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, on means placed after, so T comes beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought is careful consideration of something, which is what deliberation means.

clue.text: Spooner's low bit is over the top

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famous for swapping the starting sounds of words

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow and a touch is a small bit; swapping the opening sounds of the pair gives the phrase

explanation.surface: Spooner's poor contribution was excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of MOO and TOUCH to get the answer. Low is the cow's noise, not the opposite of high.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the top is an idiom for excessive, which is what the phrase means.

clue.text: Narrow opening in a northern river? This will provide more room

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the letters of the others
the opening of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A narrow gap by a river in the north would make space for an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England that gives Exeter its name.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an extension added to a building, which supplies extra space.

clue.text: Volunteer force's excessive enthusiasm for island state

parts.note: the TA, or Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve; with the 's

explanation.surface: Reservists have a wild passion for an island state.
explanation.walkthrough: The Territorial Army was the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island that forms one of the states of Australia.

clue.text: Puzzling child, as favourite may be

definitions.note: an adjective phrase describing the favourite's odds

explanation.surface: A baffling youngster, in the way a frontrunner might be.
explanation.definitionFit: A favourite in a race is often odds-on, meaning the betting odds are shorter than evens.

clue.text: Sap in sewer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to exhaust, sap strength from
second meaning: a pipe carrying waste water

explanation.surface: Plant fluid found in a waste pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: Sap looks like tree juice, but it is the verb meaning weaken, and sewer is the pipe rather than someone who sews.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb meaning gradually deplete and a noun for a channel taking away waste water.

clue.text: Carol is keeping mum inside — it's stifling

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one word goes inside another

explanation.surface: Someone named Carol says nothing about what is inside, and the secrecy feels oppressive.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a name and keeping mum like staying silent; carol is the verb sing and mum is mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Smothering means suffocating, which is a synonym of stifling.

clue.text: Neighbour bringing instrument back

indicators.note: back means returning to the start, so the word is read from the end

parts.note: a tuba is a brass instrument

explanation.surface: The person next door returns a borrowed musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbour looks like a noun for the person next door, but it is the verb meaning adjoin.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to share a boundary with, which is what neighbour means as a verb.

clue.text: Cricket trophy presented after 500 runs

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
the Ashes is the England-Australia Test cricket trophy

explanation.surface: A cricket prize handed over once a batsman has scored five hundred runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Runs looks like cricket scoring but is the definition: quick sprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashes are short fast runs, so the plural noun matches runs.

clue.text: Unpleasant odour from head of smelly fish

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, the one at the top

parts.note: a tench is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A bad smell comes from a rotting fish head.
explanation.definitionFit: A stench is a strong foul smell, which is an unpleasant odour.
